### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s).

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9f4b652e3a488f4351b47efdea93202033c064f7`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9f4b652e3a488f4351b47efdea93202033c064f7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `17939343c47eea434e97e6ef907caadee2cd4866` — the merge of head `f10bbe8e8aa6f4471f5dd7109c0d53b297fc84a7` into base `9f4b652e3a488f4351b47efdea93202033c064f7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 17939343c47eea434e97e6ef907caadee2cd4866 && git checkout 17939343c47eea434e97e6ef907caadee2cd4866
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9f4b652e3a488f4351b47efdea93202033c064f7 f10bbe8e8aa6f4471f5dd7109c0d53b297fc84a7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9f4b652e3a488f4351b47efdea93202033c064f7 && git merge --no-ff f10bbe8e8aa6f4471f5dd7109c0d53b297fc84a7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9f4b652e3a488f4351b47efdea93202033c064f7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9f4b652e3a488f4351b47efdea93202033c064f7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0e4fdb4e7963be8f0d92a7f392360d014852de0f`
Local-runs: none

Full record on this PR (stage W3 of #15204, the walled catalog refusal at the remaining `/packages` write doors, ADR-0131 D3). Reviewed read-only: the PR body, its 7-file list (+547 / −42), the net diff of `0e4fdb4e79` against `main` (merge base `48cca4ae00`, the commit W2 #22935 and #22939 landed under; `main` read at `6a7eca6868`, three commits past the base — `74c4b3435e`, `147a0d1acc`, `6a7eca6868` — none touching any of the PR's seven paths, only sibling semantic entries in the same directory; `mergeable` true), the 34 commits of the branch (W2's own commits and the merges of `main` sit beneath the merge base, so the three-dot diff holds exactly the seven files), card #15204's body and all 176 comments through the dev's addendum 6121258157 (among them the W3 measurement 6117740670, the seat note 6117751450, the W2 ruling 6114823168, the 17.7.0 measurement 6114989076, the Landed records 6117358377 and 6121083900, the next-prerelease rulings 6117174845, 6117531327 and 6119234024, and the D3 pointer 6070695107), W2's contract review 6117680834 on #22935 (its ③ 2 is the escalation W3 answers), ADR-0131 D3 and D6 and ADR-0087 (the launch-window section and the disposition vocabulary) as served on `main`, and on `main`: `walledCatalogWriteVerdict` (`meta-write-capability.ts`), `readEffectiveTenancyPosture`, the dispatcher's `resolveServiceOrLoud` and `classifyService`, every branch of `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` at the merge base and at the head, the precedents `06cc45dc36` (W) and `4806b18aea` (W2) with W2's `refuseWalledCatalogPackageDelete`, changeset, entry and dogfood pins, `protocol.ts`'s `publishPackageDrafts`, `discardPackageDrafts`, `discardDraftInItsScope`, `revertStoredPackage`, `duplicatePackage`, `reassignOrphanedMetadata`, `listCommits`, `revertCommit` and `rollbackToPackageCommit`, the `sys_metadata_commit` object, `MetadataManager.publishPackage`, the REST package registrar and its route ledger, the census page's #22950 state, and the 17.7.0 tree at `4e4e881427`. Nothing was built, run, re-run or ablated.

**Gate verdicts on the head, read 2026-10-12T09:35Z.** 34 check-runs: 32 `completed` — 30 `success`, 2 `skipped` (the roster skips `Console Pin Gate` and `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`) — and **2 still `in_progress`, named here as pending: `Test Core (3/6)` and `Test Core (4/6)`**; their conclusions are the gate verdicts when they land, and this record does not pre-empt them. Green among the completed: `Auto Label`, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Check Changeset`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Check PR Size`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` and its three shards, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `No other open PR may claim the same issue`, `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path`, `Part-of PR must not also close its card`, `Spec property liveness`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Test Core (1/6)`, `Test Core (2/6)`, `Test Core (5/6)`, `Test Core (6/6)`, `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · workspace`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `filter`. Where a judgment below says "pinned", the pin is one of the green runs: the dogfood shards carry `wall-package-doors-refusal.dogfood.test.ts` (21 pins) beside W2's 19 and W's 17, `Lint & Repo Gates` carries `check:system-context-census`, `Check Changeset` carries `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, and `Type Check · source gates` carries `@objectstack/spec`'s entry gates — not a local run. The PR is a draft, `mergeable` true, `mergeable_state` `blocked`; no review is submitted on it.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.

1. **The six measured doors (brief point a).** One helper, `refuseWalledCatalogPackageWrite`, generalises W2's `refuseWalledCatalogPackageDelete` (which it replaces; the W2 delete now calls it with the same stored-row reader). It resolves the effective posture through `readEffectiveTenancyPosture`, asks `walledCatalogWriteVerdict` FIRST for `SECURITY_CATALOG_TYPES[0]` with `isSystem: ec?.isSystem === true` and `callerPosture: ec?.posture` — the operator rung off the execution context, never a held capability — and returns `null` without calling `readTypes` when that answer admits (`single`, no `tenancy` service, `isSystem`, `PLATFORM_ADMIN`). Only a refused caller's items are read, and the first security-catalog type among them answers `deps.error(…, 403)`. At each door the call sits after `requireManageMetadata` and before the first write:
   - `publish-drafts`: before `resolveProtocol` and `publishPackageDrafts`; reads `sys_metadata` rows `{ package_id: id, state: 'draft' }`. `publishPackageDrafts` promotes `repo.listDrafts({ packageId })`, the environment repository's organization-less drafts — the reader is that population or a superset (a legacy organization-scoped draft, which the verb skips). **Right.**
   - `revert` (discard drafts): before `revertStoredPackage`; the same draft reader. `revertStoredPackage` discards exactly `listDrafts({ packageId })` through `discardDraftInItsScope`. **Right** for this door — and see item 2 for its sibling.
   - `rollback`: after the body parse, before `rollbackToPackageCommit`; reads the target `sys_metadata_commit` row by id, then `protocol.listCommits({ packageId: target.package_id })`, and keeps every commit other than the target whose `operation` is `apply` and whose `createdAt` is not earlier than the target's instant. `rollbackToPackageCommit` reverts, through `revertCommit`, exactly the `apply` commits strictly newer than the target of that same package, read the same way (`findOne` by id, then `listCommits`); `listCommits` returns `id`, `operation`, parsed `items` and `createdAt`, the fields the reader uses. The reader is therefore the reverted set or a superset (equal instants; an unparseable instant folds to "included"). The `operation === 'apply'` filter is exact: rollback never undoes a `revert` commit. **Right**, and the "superset of the reverted ones" claim in the body and the helper's comment is true.
   - `commits/:commitId/revert`: before `revertCommit`; reads the commit row by id and its `items` (JSON text, parsed by `commitItemTypes`, which also accepts an already-parsed array). `revertCommit` reads that row by id and reverts those items; the URL's `:id` is read by neither, as the measurement said — pinned under a URL naming A's own package. A missing commit reads as touching nothing and the verb answers its own `COMMIT_NOT_FOUND` 404. **Right.**
   - `duplicate`: after `requireDuplicableSource`, before `duplicatePackage` (whose first write is the target's `installPackage`); reads `{ package_id: id }` in every state. `duplicatePackage` copies `{ package_id, state: 'active', organization_id: null }` rows, so the reader is a superset (a source whose only catalog row is a draft is refused though nothing would be copied) — a conservative refusal, text in ③ 4. **Right.**
   - `adopt-orphans`: before `reassignOrphanedMetadata`; reads `{ organization_id: null }` rows kept when `package_id` is null, empty or `'sys_metadata'`. That is `reassignOrphanedMetadata`'s selection verbatim. **Right.**
   - The control holds by construction at every door: a `readTypes` that yields no security-catalog type returns `null`, so a catalog-free package, commit or orphan set stays admitted to the same tenant — pinned for publish-drafts, commit revert, rollback, revert and duplicate on A's own package under both postures (the catalog-free adopt-orphans case is pinned for the operator and under `single` only; ③ 4 i).

2. **Completeness (brief point b) — one door is left out, and the texts claim it: `POST /packages/:id/discard-drafts`.** Every `/packages` branch at the head was read: `GET /packages`, `POST /packages`, `GET /:id`, `PATCH /:id`, `DELETE /:id`, `PATCH /:id/enable`, `/disable`, `POST /:id/publish`, `/publish-drafts`, `/discard-drafts`, `GET /:id/commits`, `POST /:id/commits/:commitId/revert`, `/rollback`, `/revert`, `GET /:id/export`, `POST /:id/adopt-orphans`, `/duplicate`.
   - **Covered by W (on `main`):** the `/meta` item write doors (save, reset, publish, rollback) on both transports, the permission-set clone door, the data door on `sys_position` / `sys_permission_set` / `sys_capability`, and the Setup environment-door write. **By W2:** `install-local` install, upgrade and uninstall, and `DELETE /packages/:id`. **By W3:** `publish-drafts`, `revert`, `rollback`, `commits/:commitId/revert`, `duplicate`, `adopt-orphans`.
   - **Not catalog doors, by reading:** `POST /packages` (its manifest has no position or permission-set collection; W2 ① 1), `PATCH /:id` (a `name` / `description` / `version` patch through `updatePackage`, no item moves), `enable` / `disable` (the registry's enabled bit and `setPackageDisabled`; D6/D12's question, carried since W2), `POST /:id/publish` (`MetadataManager.publishPackage` publishes `collectPackageMembers` from the in-memory registry, which never holds a writable package's stored catalog rows, and `requireWritablePackage` refuses a code or installed package first), the reads and the export. REST mounts only `POST /packages/publish` (the marketplace registry publish; `rest-route-ledger.ts:457`), and no code outside `packages.ts` calls `publishPackageDrafts`, `discardPackageDrafts`, `revertCommit`, `rollbackToPackageCommit`, `duplicatePackage`, `reassignOrphanedMetadata` or `revertStoredPackage`. `metadata-protocol` asks the predicate nowhere, so nothing below a door covers one the door misses.
   - **Left out: `POST /packages/:id/discard-drafts`** (head `packages.ts:1866`), behind `requireManageMetadata` alone, with no rung and no walled check. It calls `protocol.discardPackageDrafts({ packageId })`, which lists `repo.listDrafts({ packageId })` and discards each draft through `discardDraftInItsScope` — the SAME population and the SAME per-draft step `revertStoredPackage` takes for the `revert` door this PR refuses (`protocol.ts:23599`–`23650`; the head's own `revert` comment at `packages.ts:1996` calls them "the rows discard-drafts reads"). So under `isolated` / `group`, the tenant W3 refuses at `revert` ("A discarding the operator's pending catalog draft is refused, and the draft stays") sends `discard-drafts` instead and discards the operator's pending catalog draft at `200`. The refusal W3 adds for the discard effect is bypassable by its sibling verb, and the measurement's placement (a) — "the rows these verbs promote or discard" — is executed for one of the two verbs that discard them. W2's review had named both verbs together ("`revert` and `discard-drafts` only discard drafts", 6117680834 ① 1); the W3 measurement measured `revert` alone and the seat note dispatched `revert` alone, which is why the dev's execution matches its dispatch and not the rule. 17.7.0 carries `discard-drafts` too (`4e4e881427:1792`), so the measurement's six-door reading of the release, and what #22938 was told, are short one door.
   - **Why this fails the record rather than being escalated:** unlike W2's four unmeasured doors, which W2's texts claimed nothing about, this PR's texts state the rule as closed over the discard verbs and over the `/packages` write doors as a set: the title and the changeset's title line ("the `/packages` verbs that publish, **discard**, roll back, revert, duplicate or adopt … are the platform operator's"), census row 55b ("at the `/packages` write doors (delete, `publish-drafts`, `revert`, `rollback`, `commits/:commitId/revert`, `duplicate`, `adopt-orphans`)"), `metadata-api.mdx` ("The package's other write verbs follow the same rule under a wall"), `permission-sets.mdx` ("So do the package verbs that publish, **discard**, roll back, revert, duplicate or adopt catalog items") and the body ("row 55b names the seven `/packages` write doors"). Each of those sentences is **wrong** against the code by exactly this door. Landing them would record, in the census and the docs that release-cut condition (f) and the first `next` are read against, a refusal that a sibling verb walks around.
   - **The remedy is one hunk and its texts:** at the `discard-drafts` branch, after `requireManageMetadata` and before `resolveProtocol`, `refuseWalledCatalogPackageWrite(deps, _context, 'Discarding the drafts of package "ID"', storedRowTypes(qlService, { package_id: id, state: 'draft' }))` — the `revert` door's reader, since the verbs read the same rows; a refusal pin under `isolated` and `group` (the draft stays), the operator and `single` controls extended by the verb, and the door's own ablation; the changeset gains its FROM → TO bullet, the entry's `surface` and `acceptanceCriteria` name it, row 55b lists it, the two docs pages add the verb, and the 17.7.0 note names `discard-drafts` beside the six.

3. **Envelope (brief point c).** All six doors are dispatcher doors and answer `deps.error(…, 403)`, this transport's `PERMISSION_DENIED`, with the message `ACTION is refused: it touches security catalog items.` followed by the predicate's own sentence, which names the posture in quotes and `ADR-0131 D3` — the pins assert status, code, the quoted posture and the ADR together. That is the split W fixed and W2 kept: `FORBIDDEN` at the REST doors, `PERMISSION_DENIED` at the dispatcher. **Consistent.** The W2 delete's sentence changes from "the package carries security catalog items" to "it touches security catalog items"; W2's delete pin asserts the posture only, so no landed pin moves (text, ③ 4 iv).

4. **Controls (brief point d).** `single`: `postureEnforcesWall` is false, the predicate admits, `readTypes` is never called; the `single` suite has the same sub-operator `manage_metadata` holder run all six verbs on the operator's catalog-carrying package at `200` — unchanged. The operator: admitted on the `PLATFORM_ADMIN` rung, pinned on its own catalog-carrying package through every verb under both postures. No `tenancy` service: `classifyService` folds a not-registered service to `never-registered`, `resolveServiceOrLoud` to `undefined`, `effectiveTenancyPosture(undefined)` to `undefined`, which the predicate admits — inert. A registered `tenancy` service that cannot answer: `classifyService` rethrows any other failure, `readEffectiveTenancyPosture` wraps it in `AuthzStoreUnavailableError`, the helper's `try` wraps only `readTypes`, so the throw reaches `handlePackagesRequest`'s outer catch and `errorFromThrown`, which keeps the error's own 503. **Refused, never admitted**, the shape W and W2 landed. The consequence W2's review named for the delete now holds at six more doors: with a failing posture service, every one of them refuses before its items are read, a catalog-free write under `single` included — the activation gate's shape, not a defect.

5. **Pins and ablations (brief point e).** 21 tests: per walled posture, the guard, one refusal pin for each of publish-drafts, revert, rollback, duplicate and adopt-orphans, two for the commit revert (the operator's package URL and A's own), the catalog-free control and the operator control (10 × 2), plus the `single` control. Each refusal pin compares B's resolution across its own request only, re-establishes the state it needs (the `revert` pin re-saves the draft before refusing), and asserts the non-movement that matters for its verb (B's grants, the draft row, the empty target package, the orphan's `package_id`). The ablation table (publish-drafts 2, revert 2, rollback 2, commit revert 4, duplicate 2, adopt-orphans 2; W2's 19 green throughout) is read as reported and not re-measured; the counts match the pin counts above, and the dogfood shards are green on this head. Per 6117751450 the six dispatched doors each carry refusal pins under both postures with the operator and `single` controls — met; the seventh door of item 2 has none because it has no refusal.

6. **The spec entry and the changeset (brief point f).**
   - `18.walled-catalog-package-verbs-retired.ts`: the semantic shape (`id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`) under protocol major 18 beside W's and W2's entries; the registry is generated, so no index is owed; `surface` carries no backticks and names the six doors with the condition each is judged by, the "whatever package the URL names" clause included; `replacement`, `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria` read as the code behaves (the operator rung, the catalog-free package, `single`, the per-verb non-movement). **Right** for the six it names; it does not name `discard-drafts` (item 2). One overclaim in `acceptanceCriteria`: "the same owner runs every verb on a package of their own whose items carry no catalog item with 200" — the file pins that for five verbs, not for adopt-orphans (③ 4 i).
   - The changeset: `minor` for `@objectstack/runtime` (the door code) and `@objectstack/spec` (the entry) — the two published packages the diff moves; `@objectstack/qa/dogfood` is private and `content/docs` owes none. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on its own line; the `**BREAKING**` banner; the marker `registered walled-catalog-package-verbs-retired`, an id that resolves and is new in the diff (`Check Changeset` green). The FROM → TO bullets, each read against its door: publish-drafts and revert "when the package has a pending position or permission-set draft" — the draft reader; rollback "when a commit it would undo touched one" — the reverted set or its equal-instant superset; the commit revert "the commit's own items are judged … the URL's package segment changes nothing" — exact; duplicate "when the source package holds one" — the stored rows; adopt-orphans "when the environment's orphaned rows include one" — exact. The "Unchanged" paragraph (the catalog-free package, the operator, `single`, no `tenancy` service, "no extra read happens: the verdict is asked before the items are read") is true of the items; the posture itself is resolved for every caller, a service resolve, the reading W2 accepted. The remedy names the entry, the predicate and the shared helper. **Right**, except that its title line claims the discard verbs (item 2).

7. **Docs and census (brief point g).** `metadata-api.mdx`: the six-verb list under the delete section, each verb with what it is judged by, reads against the code — **right** — but its lead sentence "The package's other write verbs follow the same rule under a wall" is **wrong** by `discard-drafts`. `permission-sets.mdx`: "So do the package verbs that publish, discard, roll back, revert, duplicate or adopt catalog items (`publish-drafts`, `revert`, …)" — **wrong** by the same verb; the "refuse any other caller `403` before anything changes" clause is true of the six. `system-context.mdx` row 55b: the door list adds the six beside the delete and the anchor moves to `packages.ts#refuseWalledCatalogPackageWrite`, a symbol that exists at the head with the one `ec?.isSystem` read W2 anchored (moved, none added; `Lint & Repo Gates`, which carries `check:system-context-census`, is green); the row's "when the items they act on include a position or a permission set" says two types where the code counts `capability` too (W2 ③ 4 ii, unchanged). **No count line is reintroduced:** the diff touches only row 55b, and #22950's `5f4e8a544c` state of the page stands on `main`.

8. **No collateral (brief point h).** No `CHANGELOG.md`, no `content/docs/releases/`, no `pnpm-lock.yaml`, no `docs/adr/**`. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

- The diff publishes an accept-set narrowing at six dispatcher doors (BREAKING, shipped `minor` under ADR-0087's launch-window rule, which `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` enforces and `Check Changeset` is green on), and in `@objectstack/spec` one semantic entry. No export, type, dependency edge or manifest changes. The changeset grades exactly those two packages `minor`, carries the banner, the `registered` marker and `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`; the PR body carries the same line on its third line, after `Part of #15204` and a blank line, the placement accepted for W and W2. **The level matches what the diff publishes, and so does the Clause-② line.** The seventh door of ① 2 changes neither: refusing it is the same narrowing at one more door of the same package, `minor` under the same rule, inside the same entry.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry, answered or escalated.

1. **The dev's addendum 6121258157** (head `0e4fdb4e79`, `open_questions: []`, `out_of_scope_findings: []`). Its one deviation — the branch carries W2's commits and two merges of `main` beneath the merge — is verified: the net diff against the merge base holds exactly the seven files of the PR's own list and no hunk of W2's, and `main`'s three later commits touch none of those paths. Its summary line "Census row 55b names the seven `/packages` write doors" is the overclaim of ① 2.
2. **FAIL reason, the one condition of this verdict: `POST /packages/:id/discard-drafts` (① 2).** A live door, in the same file, behind the same gate, discarding the same rows through the same protocol step as the `revert` door this PR refuses, left admitted to a walled tenant, while the title, the changeset's title line, census row 55b and both docs pages state the rule as closed over the discard verbs and the `/packages` write doors. Fix it in this PR as ① 2's remedy says, with its pins and ablation, and name it in the 17.7.0 note for #22938. The measured doors, the helper, the envelope, the controls, the level and the entry stand as reviewed; a delta review of the added hunk, pins and texts is all the next round owes.
3. **Carried, unchanged:** whether a walled organization's `manage_metadata` may author or publish the environment's non-catalog metadata through these doors (the PR's acceptance notes; 6114823168 and 6117680834 ③ 3). The maintainer's. And the `adopt-orphans` note in the acceptance notes — any catalog orphan refuses the whole adoption, because the verb rebinds every orphan at once — is the measured placement (e)'s first alternative; the seat may still choose its second ("leave catalog types out of the adoption under a wall"), which is a different accept set and would need its own measurement and texts.
4. **For the seat, text only, none moving the accept set or the level:** (i) the catalog-free control for a tenant under a wall does not include `adopt-orphans` (the harness's `ENV_SET` orphan would refuse it), so the test title, the file header and the entry's `acceptanceCriteria` say "every verb" where five are pinned; a sentence, or a catalog-free orphan fixture. (ii) `duplicate`'s reader counts draft and organization-scoped rows that `duplicatePackage` would not copy; a `state: 'active'` filter would make it exact, and the body's "the source's stored rows" is true as written.
